annotations.text:
Expected XI — four directions, real GW1 data (Arsenal v Coventry).

The case for the page: the chart says Timber 86% at RB and Saliba 96% at RCB. Both are injured, so the shirts go to White (0.83) and Mosquera (0.94). Nothing on the site shows that today.

A · The default view: the eleven who will actually start, gold-edged where someone has stepped in.

For — reads in one glance, and the pitch does the positional work for free.
Against — the men behind the starter are invisible, and it says nothing about how close a call a slot was.

B · The same pitch, but the DIFF is the subject: forecast starter struck through, replacement beneath.

For — answers the question that made us build this, and the gain is stated in points.
Against — a squad with no injuries has nothing to show, so the page is empty most weeks.

C · No pitch. Every slot with its full depth as rows.

For — shows the players behind the starter and the exact split when two men share a slot; survives a phone without redrawing.
Against — loses the spatial read entirely; you have to know that RCB sits next to LCB.

D · Not a page — a card for the existing Teams route.

For — reaches readers who would never open a lineup page, and costs no new nav.
Against — the pitch is too small to carry numbers, so it defers to a fuller view anyway.
